proposition: She has sold herself into the Mercy Academy and is bound for a ten-year term
quote: I had consented.

proposition: The Academy annually intakes one hundred girls
quote: The hundred benches were arranged like a small amphitheatre; families sat in the outer rings, sober as undertakers.

proposition: Only three of each intake leave after their ten-year term
quote: "Out of the hundred who enter each year," she said, "only three leave at the end of their ten-year term. The rest remain under the Academy's charge as is recorded."

proposition: She signed the Contract with a handwritten signature that the scribe copied into the Folio
quote: I signed in a hand that had practised keeping accounts in cramped ledgers. The scribe copied it into the Folio in ink that smelled of iron and permanence.

proposition: Her signature was witnessed by the Headmistress, who made a mark beside it
quote: The Headmistress dipped a fingertip and made a mark beside the signature — her witness.

proposition: The Contract's text is not quoted in the prose and thus the exact wording is unknown
quote: The Contract's clause was quiet in the packet but not shy: ten years. The writing named it without flourish — a span not measured in noble phrase but in the clear currency of years.

proposition: She believes the Academy enforces ten-year terms and that leaving is rare
quote: "Out of the hundred who enter each year," she said, "only three leave at the end of their ten-year term. The rest remain under the Academy's charge as is recorded."

proposition: The Bell signals meals, lessons, and curfew as part of the Academy schedule
quote: The Bell's note came through the open doorway like a hand laid on your shoulder. It sounded for meals; it sounded for lessons; it sounded for curfew.

proposition: Chores are assigned by rota posted beneath the intake list
quote: Chores were given by a rota posted beneath the intake list: garden, laundry, kitchen, and the little jobs...

proposition: The dormitory assigns bunks and posts assignment board; staff assign placements
quote: "Assigned by staff," the woman who led us said... The board held our numbers; people counted themselves into a place like a census.

proposition: Discipline is enforced by small marks in an unseen ledger and courteous correction; exact punishments are not described
quote: Discipline showed itself in small ways: the softness of the woman's voice when she told us what to do, the careful way the head of the dorm would mark a failing with a line on a ledger we could not see, the curt remark that carried the edge of consequence.

proposition: She believes the dormitory's rules are work, witness, record, and that methods of enforcement will be learned later
quote: The rules of the House had been set out plainly: work, witness, record. The ways it was enforced would be learned later; for now the rota and the list were enough to tell me where I stood.

proposition: She wrote 'sold' as her provenance on the Contract and thus considers herself sold.
quote: When she set the pen to the Contract she wrote 'sold' in the space the Folio called Provenance.

proposition: The Contract binds her for ten years and promises education, shelter, and apprenticeship.
quote: The Contract's clause was quiet in the packet but not shy: ten years. The Contract promised education and shelter and apprenticeship, the learning of trades and the promise of a place to stand after ten years.

proposition: Out of one hundred entrants each year, only three leave after ten years; the rest remain under the Academy's charge.
quote: “Out of the hundred who enter each year, only three leave at the end of their ten-year term. The rest remain under the Academy's charge as is recorded.”

proposition: The Folio serves as record and law for the Academy.
quote: “So entered under the charge of the Mercy Academy. Let the Folio stand as record and law.

proposition: The Folio is kept in Archive and a day's intake is transcribed and posted publicly beneath it.
quote: The list was already up when we came in: a narrow column of names pinned beneath the Folio’s page, the rest of the book gone for the afternoon as if it were too heavy for public eyes.

proposition: The House counts things as work, witness, record.
quote: In the dark she thought of how the house counted things: work, witness, record.

proposition: The Binding Seal is displayed behind glass in the Ink Room and is not to be touched.
quote: Behind the glass the seal looked like a small, round relic, a mound of beeswax capped by a dark iron signet... The scribe's finger tapped the display with a care that felt like punctuation; no one touched the seal. Loren's voice, low, said only what could be said: "You see its order. You do not lift the seal."

proposition: A tacit tally system exists where instructors mark owed favors or debts in ledgers.
quote: He did not scold; he slid a marked tally into the others' ledger with a pen whose scratch she could not see. Rue felt the quick weight of owing.

proposition: The Three's stories function as a mix of warning and example used to enforce conformity and expectation.
quote: Stories about the Three were told to us as if they were both threat and promise... The Three meant more in the telling than in any fact: miracle, commodity, closed mouth.

proposition: She sold herself to stop her family's debts and promised to provide shelter and reduce the ledger's burden.
quote: She had promised, not with a seal but with a whisper beside her mother's pillow, to make the numbers stop climbing... 'I will stand where there is a roof.'

proposition: There is an institutional practice of excusal slips stamped by the dormmistress to excuse duties temporarily, with make-up chores assigned later.
quote: She took Aya's wrist... and then pinned an excusal slip to Aya's trunk: a thin parchment stamped with the dormmistress's cipher. It was an official exemption that would keep Aya from the garden rota that afternoon but note an extra wash shift to be made up at week's end.

proposition: The Binding Seal makes Contract claims enforceable and is used to ensure promises are kept; enforcement is framed as a tool of reliability by the Headmistress.
quote: "The Binding Seal is not theatre. It makes claims enforceable when we must ensure a promise is kept. But enforcement is not a wolf at the door; it is a tool of reliability."

proposition: Departures are accounted for and recorded when rightly earned; the Folio is consulted when obligations are complete or for review.
quote: "The Folio is our record. Its pages are consulted when the house's obligations are complete and when there is cause for review. Departures are not casual things; they are accounted for and recorded when they are rightly earned."

proposition: The Headmistress's public rhetoric hides a private calculus; the Headmistress's language suggests margins and logs exist that make promises practicable but are not publicized.
quote: The Headmistress's voice was the voice the town heard at the Folio... 'In the margins, we record the particulars that make those promises practicable: orders of apprenticeship, sponsorships, and the logs the house keeps to see a term through.'

proposition: Apprenticeship assignments are recorded in house logs (scribal log, folded slips pinned to trunks) and sponsorships/training hours are noted in those logs.
quote: At the long table, a scribe had unrolled a narrow log—its columns already filled with shifted names and notes... 'Sponsorship is noted in the logs; training hours recorded.'

proposition: Discrepancies in the Folio (crossings-out, marginal scours, added cramped marginalia) indicate possible erasure or later edits; these are explainable by scribal differences but may also signal deliberate alteration.
quote: On the page something had been altered... ink density like tide marks, a careful crossing-out..., and a faint, scoured smear at the margin...

proposition: The Headmistress will deflect questions about the Folio's discrepancies and recommend formal complaint; her pattern is naming procedure rather than showing margins.
quote: The Headmistress... 'We maintain our records with care... sometimes a note is compressed into a margin for administrative reasons. These are not, in themselves, conspiracies.'

proposition: The marginal word 'tethering' suggests a binding that ties obligations to a person's name and may impose costs tracked by house logs (time, trade).
quote: 'tethering'... 'It ties people to an obligation of service and craft,' he said... 'What it costs depends on what the house logs against a name. Often it's time. Often it's trade.'

proposition: The Folio and its margins continue to be sources of anomalies over time; marginal crossing-outs and cramped additions recur and the Ink Room preserves and re-hides decisions.
quote: Occasionally the Folio's margins whispered back. Rue would catch a clerk's fingers tracing a line in a closed book, or see a note pinned that did not appear on the thin public list. Sometimes the crossing-out she had once peered at in a single page reappeared in other hands: an erasure here, a cramped marginal addition there.

proposition: The War Envoy delivered notice that the war seeks the island and will return in ten days for a formal answer; the Academy will need to account for the war in its ledgers.
quote: He placed a folded paper on the lectern... 'This is notice,' he said. 'We will return in ten days for a formal answer.'

proposition: The Headmistress intends to protect the house's people by offering counted things (kitchens, shelter) and using records to bargain rather than handing over people.
quote: 'We will shelter those under our charge,' the Headmistress said... 'And we will account it. We will keep a record—who is housed, who is fed, what is pledged.'

proposition: External sponsors and port-ledger claims can impose obligations on returned alum that are not recorded in the Folio; these external accounts may demand names, hours, or other non-monetary returns.
quote: "Sponsors keep accounts that have teeth... the world outside keeps accounts that are not always written in the Folio's neat hand."

proposition: Binding hours into a civic pledge risks converting apprentices' training time into obligations that may harm their craft; ledgers can be repurposed by external parties.
quote: "If we promise labour, the girls will lose hours for their apprenticeships. That reduces their trade, not only their time."

proposition: The civic pledge recorded during the siege will function as a clear record that outsiders and negotiators can read, making counts legible and potentially actionable by external parties.
quote: The scribe removed a clean vellum and, following the Headmistress's instructions, pencilled a margin note: 'Civic pledge in effect—kitchens and labour rotation active.' It was not an enchantment; it was a document, and the document itself would be the thing negotiators read later.

proposition: Marginal notes like 'Exchange noted' indicate external sponsor ledgers that may contain the terms of departures; these marginalia change the meaning of the Folio's records by linking names to other accounts.
quote: 'Exchange noted'... 'That is the language of sponsors—an account recorded in another book.'

proposition: The 'Pending Release' Folio entry creates a formal, witnessed path for sponsors' claims to be reclassified as satisfied by civic exchange; this may allow named apprentices to petition counsel for release.
quote: 'Pending Release — conditional upon sponsor or municipal acknowledgment; civic exchange recorded.' ... 'Those with claims satisfied by civic exchange may petition counsel for release.'
